surface_summary: Margaret Odell, a Broadway beauty known as the Canary, was strangled in her apartment during a supposed burglary. The side door was bolted from the inside, and no one was seen entering or leaving except her escort, Kenneth Spotswoode, who had a solid alibi. Fingerprints of Tony Skeel, a burglar, were found, and suspicion initially fell on him and Jessup, a telephone operator.
accepted_facts: Margaret Odell was strangled in her apartment late at night.
The side door to the building was bolted from the inside all night.
Tony Skeel’s fingerprints were found in the apartment and he had a criminal record.
Kenneth Spotswoode had a verified alibi during the time of the murder.
inferred_conclusions: Tony Skeel was the murderer acting alone.
The side door was never unlocked during the night of the murder.
Kenneth Spotswoode was innocent due to his alibi.
mechanism_description: Kenneth Spotswoode planned and executed the murder to prevent Margaret Odell from ruining his life through blackmail. He staged the crime to appear as a burglary, using a phonograph record to fake screams heard by witnesses. He manipulated the side door bolt using a string and tweezers device to create an alibi, and killed Tony Skeel, who had witnessed the murder and attempted to blackmail him.
delivery_path: Spotswoode unbolted the side door using a string and tweezers device to enter unnoticed.
He hid in the apartment until the victim and her escort arrived.
He strangled Margaret Odell while Tony Skeel hid in the clothes-press.
Spotswoode staged a burglary by ransacking the apartment and removing jewelry.
He set a phonograph record with screams to play after leaving to fake a call for help.
He rebolted the side door using the string and tweezers device to create an alibi.
He killed Tony Skeel later to silence him and prevent blackmail.
outcome_result: Kenneth Spotswoode is arrested for the murder of Margaret Odell and subsequently commits suicide.

false_assumption.statement: The side door was bolted from the inside all night, making entry or exit impossible.
false_assumption.why_it_seems_reasonable: The janitor and witnesses confirmed the door was bolted, and no one was seen entering or leaving through it. The telephone operators on duty also denied any unauthorized passage.
false_assumption.what_it_hides: The door was manipulated by a mechanical device operated from outside, allowing the murderer to enter and exit without being seen and then rebolt the door, creating a false impression of security.

supporting_points: Jessup was the only person who could have unlocked and rebolted the side door.
He had a motive of jealousy and love for the victim.
His fingerprints were found in the apartment.
He was caught trying to pawn stolen jewelry.
false_solution.the_one_flaw: The mechanical device used by Spotswoode allowed him to manipulate the side door without Jessup’s involvement, and Jessup had no opportunity to commit the murder.

red_herrings.description: Tony Skeel, a known burglar with fingerprints in the apartment, was suspected of the murder and robbery.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: His criminal record and presence in the apartment during the murder time.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: He was hiding in the clothes-press and witnessed the murder but did not commit it; he was later killed by the real murderer to silence him.

red_herrings.description: Dr. Lindquist was infatuated and jealous of the victim and threatened her, making him a suspect.
red_herrings.points_at_suspect: His threats and unstable behavior suggested possible motive.
red_herrings.innocent_explanation: He had a solid alibi being hospitalized during the murder and was not physically capable of committing the crime.

closed_circle.rationale: These four men were the only ones intimately connected with the victim and had motives or opportunity; others were excluded by alibis or lack of connection.

inference_path.correction: Side door was manipulated by a mechanical device operated from outside.
inference_path.effect: Allowed murderer to enter and exit unnoticed, creating false alibi.

inference_path.observation: Phonograph record played screams and calls for help after escort left.
inference_path.correction: Record was pre-recorded by Spotswoode to fake screams and calls.
inference_path.effect: Created alibi for Spotswoode and misled witnesses.
required_evidence: Phonograph record found in victim’s apartment
Vance’s analysis of record timing and mechanism

inference_path.observation: Fingerprints of Tony Skeel found in apartment.
inference_path.correction: Skeel was hiding in the clothes-press and witnessed the murder.
inference_path.effect: Skeel was a witness, not the murderer.

Skeel’s testimony and behavior under questioning

inference_path.observation: Jessup was the only one who could unlock and rebolt the side door.
inference_path.correction: Jessup was an impostor and not involved in the murder; door manipulation was by Skeel.
inference_path.effect: Jessup’s arrest was a false solution.
required_evidence: Jessup’s real identity as Benton with criminal record

inference_path.observation: Spotswoode had a solid alibi playing poker until 3 a.m.
inference_path.correction: Spotswoode’s alibi was fabricated; he committed the murder and arranged the alibi.
inference_path.effect: Spotswoode is the true murderer despite apparent alibi.
required_evidence: Psychological analysis of Spotswoode’s behavior during poker

inference_path.observation: Victim’s gown was torn and jewelry stolen in a typical burglary manner.
inference_path.correction: The burglary was staged by Spotswoode to disguise the murder motive.
inference_path.effect: Robbery was a cover-up for murder.
required_evidence: Condition of jewel-case and poker used to fake forced entry
Testimony of maid and witnesses about apartment disorder

inference_path.observation: Skeel was blackmailing Spotswoode and was later murdered.
inference_path.correction: Spotswoode killed Skeel to silence him and cover up the crime.
required_evidence: Spotswoode’s confession and circumstances of Skeel’s murder

discriminating_test.design: Vance demonstrated the side door manipulation by using tweezers tied to a string to unbolt and rebolt the door from outside without being seen. The phonograph record was played to simulate screams and calls for help timed to the murder. A staged poker game was used to analyze psychological traits of suspects.
discriminating_test.knowledge_revealed: The test revealed how the murderer could enter and exit undetected, create a mechanical alibi, and the psychological profile matching the true culprit.
discriminating_test.pass_condition: Successful unlocking and relocking of the side door by mechanical means without detection, and psychological behavior consistent with the murderer during the poker game.

fair_play_explanation: The reader is provided with all physical evidence, witness testimonies, and the layout of the apartment, including the side door and the clothes-press. The presence of the phonograph record and its timing is described in detail. The psychological profiles and alibis of suspects are fully explored. The mechanical device used to manipulate the door is demonstrated before the solution is revealed, allowing the attentive reader to deduce the method and suspect.
